description: We are team of youth challengers, together we're Nebula Astrologist Union XVI but for short, NAUXVI. My team are passionate into diving deeper about learning new thing, every member skilled in many ways such as anything mentioned with STEM activities. Not only that, our mission for this challenge are, identifying and characterize new terrestrial analogs for future bases or landing sites by presenting the findings as a map with a research from a worldwide agencies to figure out how to solve it.
summary: To enable safe, cost-effective pre-flight validation of habitats, rovers, and life-support systems for future deep-space exploration, our team, Nebula Astrologist Union XVI, developed a quantitative framework for identifying terrestrial analog sites on Earth that mirror the Lunar South Pole and Mars (Jezero Crater and Arcadia Planitia). By cross-referencing five years of NASA Earth observation datasets (MODIS, SRTM, Landsat 9) against lunar and Martian orbital archives (LRO and MRO) through a Geospatial Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis, the team established the Analog Fidelity Index (AFI)—a customizable, mission-weighted scoring rubric that eliminates subjective site selection while the importance that it gave are transparently accounting for Earth’s gravitational, atmospheric, and radiation boundaries. This investigation pinpointed three high-value terrestrial testbeds like, Maria Elena South in the Atacama Desert, Chile and this open-access catalog provides space agencies, commercial aerospace partners, and researchers with a reproducible roadmap to rigorously stress-test off-world technologies on Earth before launch. This way, our project able to help the researchers and scientist to use our team project as their reference for finding a better analogue sites on Earth, followed by Moon and Mars.

With the use of Gemini, we are able to finish this project in time, and I hope details inserted in the document will reach out to every researcher with curiosity out there.
